record_kind_meaning: A companion measurement record for a packaged artifact. The release record itself is docs/releases/v0.1.0.json, and the seven-element check in scripts/release_record.py applies to that file, not to this one.

frozen_backend.tree_sha256_procedure: sha256 over a canonical listing of the tree: one line per file, sorted by POSIX relative path, each line "<file sha256>  <file bytes>  <relative path>\n", the whole listing encoded as UTF-8.
frozen_backend.tree_sha256_scope: the freeze output tree only; it carries no __pycache__ (checked), so the digest describes the freeze and not the interpreter's cache of it.
frozen_backend.packaged_tree_sha256_meaning: The freeze tree and the copy the installer carries at resources/backend/labcairn measured the same digest, so the installer carries this freeze byte for byte.

web_bundle.tree_sha256_procedure: The frozen backend's tree_sha256_procedure, applied to the bundle tree.
web_bundle.packaged_tree_sha256_meaning: The bundle built from web/ and the copy the installer carries at resources/web-dist measured the same digest, so the installer carries the frontend of this commit byte for byte.

build.produced_at_meaning: The installer's own last-write timestamp, read from the produced file.
build.dist_dir_meaning: Packaging products and logs live outside the tracked tree; the artifact itself is not committed, only its measurement.
build.commands_note: The last command is the package.json script "dist": "electron-builder --win"; the run invoked electron-builder's CLI directly with the same environment. "node shell/node_modules/electron/install.js" is explicit because electron 45.2.3 ships no postinstall script and the binary is otherwise not fetched. PyInstaller is a freeze-time tool and stays out of pyproject.toml by the project's own decision, so it is installed into the project virtualenv rather than declared.
build.notes: The build ran from a git worktree whose tree is byte-identical to main at the recorded commit (git diff --stat main -- . is empty and git status --porcelain is empty), so the artifact carries the source of that commit. The packaging guard shell/scripts/require-package-inputs.mjs ran as the beforeBuild hook and did not refuse: the web bundle and the frozen backend were both present, the latter with its migrations tree.

source_evidence.worktree_tree_equals_main: git diff --stat main -- . is empty and git status --porcelain is empty, so the built tree is main's tree at the recorded commit.
source_evidence.note: The freeze carries this tree's product code: the bundle's carried material data (src/labcairn/material, added as data files by shell/scripts/build-backend-freeze.mjs) measured the same digest as this worktree's src/labcairn/material. The digests are measured over tracked source files; the main checkout's copy of the same directory also holds gitignored __pycache__ bytecode, which is not product source and is not part of any digest recorded here.

measurement.method: sha256 over the installer's bytes, measured three independent ways on the produced file
tools: python hashlib.sha256 over the file in 64 KiB blocks (the procedure scripts/release_record.py:sha256_file uses)

notes: The installer is unsigned by design (W28); the build log records "no code signing certificate configured, signing is skipped" for every executable it produced.

The installer's own name and its declared product version carry the shell package's version line, 0.0.3, because shell/package.json was not bumped for the v0.1.0 workbench release. The workbench itself is version 0.1.0 (pyproject.toml, src/labcairn/__init__.py, API_VERSION in src/labcairn/api/app.py). This measurement window did not change shell/package.json; the version bump is the owner's call.

The artifact is not reproducible from this digest alone: an NSIS build embeds a timestamp, so a rebuild produces different bytes. The digest identifies the artifact measured here, and the frozen backend's digest is the reproducible part of the build.
